sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
The window is a steady compounding story rather than a step change: growth ran 9.7% in FY2018 and 10.1% in FY2026, with the only real surge in FY2021 and FY2022 [D42][D434][D189][D238].
FY2021 net sales rose 17.5% on a 16% comparable sales increase, with e-commerce comparable sales up 44% [D189][P54].
FY2022 added 15.8% as comparable sales rose 14%, with the strongest increases in gasoline, business centers and travel [D238][P42].
Growth then settled to 6.8% in FY2023 and 5.0% in FY2024 before re-accelerating to 8.2% and 10.1% [D287][D336][D385][D434].
The United States segment supplied 7.2pp of revenue growth in FY2026 and was 72.5% of revenue [D672][D670].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, of which comparable sales were $22.5 billion, driven by 5% higher average ticket and 3% more shopping frequency [P14].
Warehouse ancillary and other businesses grew 19.9% and contributed 3.7pp, while Food and Sundries added 2.6pp on 6.6% growth [D600][D601][D559][D560].
Membership fee revenue rose 11.0% on new sign-ups, fee increases and Executive upgrades, with renewal rates of 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada [D664][P13].
Operating income grew 12.5% against 10.1% revenue growth in FY2026, an incremental margin of 4.7% [D435][D434][D457].
Operating margin reached 3.9% in FY2026, its window high, against a 3.4% median and 3.1% low [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp: SG&A added 0.1pp and cost of revenue was flat, with SG&A at 9.0% of revenue [D447][D460][D459][D414].
Gross margin fell three basis points, as a 19bp gain in warehouse ancillary and other businesses was offset by an 11bp decline in core merchandise [P12].
SG&A fell 10bp as a share of sales, though foreign-currency moves added $126 million of expense [P9].
Net margin of 3.0% sits below the 3.9% operating margin because the 24.7% effective tax rate takes $3.0 billion of the $12.3 billion pretax income [F52][F32][D420][X90][X80].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income, and free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x, above the 0.99x window median [F82][F42][D421][F102][D422][D701].
The FY2026 operating cash increase was driven by higher operating income and a reduced net investment in merchandise inventories from faster turns and better supplier terms [P6].
Free cash flow margin was 3.1%, against a 2.8% median and a 1.5% low in FY2022 [D418][D698][D696].
Capex of $6.4 billion was 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A, the highest multiple in the window [F92][D417][D423].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, or 5.0% of revenue, the 100th percentile against a retail peer median of -4.4% net cash (n=6) [D427][D428][D715][D716].
Cash and investments rose 39.4% to $21.3 billion while total debt was $6.2 billion [D453][D425][D426].
Buybacks and dividends of $3.3 billion absorbed 35.2% of free cash flow, with $848 million of repurchases leaving $1.1 billion on the authorization [D429][D430][X110][P3].
The diluted share count was essentially flat at 444.4 million, so EPS growth of 14.0% tracked net income growth of 13.9% [X100][D438][D436].
Operating margin of 3.9% ranks in the 17th percentile of six retail peers against a 5.0% median, so the model runs on volume, not margin [F32][D709][D710].
Capex has grown 17.0% in FY2026 and capex/D&A has climbed to 2.41x, so free cash flow depends on holding the current capex pace [D441][D423].
The current portion of debt jumped to $2.2 billion from $75 million, a refinancing item to track rather than an earnings problem [X160][X159].
Watch operating margin against the 3.9% FY2026 high; a print below the 3.4% median would reverse the margin trend [F32][D691][D692].
Watch free cash flow margin against the 3.1% FY2026 level and the 2.8% median; a drop toward the 1.5% FY2022 low would signal capex or working-capital strain [D418][D698][D696].
Watch membership fee growth against the 11.0% FY2026 rate, since renewal rates of 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada underpin the fee stream [D664][P13].
